result.title: Video World Models Need Predictable Latents
result.summary: Video world models trained on large-scale robot data promise a safe and scalable approach for learning and evaluating policies that act in the physical world. However, they still struggle with long-horizon rollouts and out-of-distribution generalization, and they remain computationally demanding at inference time. Typically, video world models make predictions in the latent space of a reconstruction-trained autoencoder, which however is not directly optimized for dynamics modeling. On the other hand, world models designed for latent planning usually optimize latents to be predictable, but they forgo accurate prediction of observations in pixel space. In this paper, we show that it is possible to achieve the best of both worlds: a latent geometry optimized to make future prediction as simple as possible without sacrificing accurate prediction of future observations. More precisely, we find that temporal objectives for representation learning, paired with a past-conditioned decoder architecture, lead to consistent improvements in generative video world models at the same training budget. The gains include up to 5x cheaper inference, over 7x faster training, and 15-24% lower pixel and perceptual errors out of distribution and over long horizons. Our world models also agree more closely with real-world policy evaluation when using a vision-language model to judge task success from their pixel-space predictions. Overall, our study indicates that temporal predictability is an important design criterion for the latent space of video world models, and provides concrete guidance on how to incorporate it into the training of autoencoders.

AI.brief_summary: 研究视频世界模型的 latent 空间设计，提出用时间预测目标配合 past-conditioned decoder，使 latent 既便于未来预测又保留像素重建精度，从而降低推理与训练成本并改善长时和分布外预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 「可预测 latent 几何 + 不牺牲视觉细节」的训练思路可供核查是否适用于 LVR 内部视觉状态，尤其涉及信息坍缩与长时状态更新；但对象是视频世界模型而非 VLM 推理，迁移效果需验证。
